VibePascal -- notes for CONSUMERS of the Linux compiler
Written cy1115 (2026-09-11).  Mirrored into no tarball on purpose, so it can be
corrected without contradicting bytes that are already published.

================================================================
DO NOT INVOKE THE COMPILER FROM ITS OWN SOURCE DIRECTORY
================================================================

Run the Linux compiler from a directory that contains NO .pas files.

    good:  $VP_DIR/bin/ppcx64          <- what the dist tarballs give you
    bad:   $VP_DIR/compiler/ppcx64     <- the build output, sitting in its own source tree

FPC appends the running binary's own directory to the unit search path, after
everything the caller passed.  That is documented, long-standing, correct
behaviour and it is the right thing for a compiler building its own RTL -- there
is no compiler bug here and nothing about it is going to change.

The consequence is entirely about WHERE THE BINARY LIVES.  `make -C compiler`
writes ppcx64 into compiler/, which also holds 207 .pas files.  So anyone who
invokes $VP_DIR/compiler/ppcx64 by that path silently gets 207 of the
compiler's own units prepended to their search path.  They never asked for
them, and nothing in the output says they are there.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY COSTS
----------------------
Measured against a Lazarus tree: 3 of our 207 unit names collide with its 4017
-- `compiler`, `macho`, `tokens`.  That is a small surface, and one of them
fires.  Lazarus has components/fpdebug/macho.pas (2101 lines); we have
compiler/macho.pas (2106 lines).  LazDebuggerFp gets fpdebug's OUTPUT directory
on its unit path but not fpdebug's SOURCE directory, so while that package
compiles, the only macho.pas FPC can see is OURS.  It recompiles unit `macho`
into LazDebuggerFp's output directory with a different CRC (62128 B vs
62168 B), which invalidates fpimgreadermachofile.ppu, and the IDE build dies:

    Fatal: (10022) Can't find unit FpImgReaderMachoFile used by FpImgReaderMacho

The failure names a LAZARUS unit and reads like a Lazarus problem from end to
end.  It cost LazarusDeveloper three cycles and a completely unbuildable
x86_64-linux/gtk2 IDE before a -vut trace showed the real line:

    Searching file .../vibepascal/compiler/macho.pas... found

Same binary, copied into an empty directory, everything else identical: rc=0.
If you are chasing a "can't find unit" whose named unit plainly exists in your
own tree, run with -vut and grep the trace for vibepascal/compiler.

WHAT WE SHIP, AND WHAT YOU HAVE TO DO
-------------------------------------
THE PUBLISHED TARBALLS WERE NEVER AFFECTED.  Every Linux dist tarball
(linux64, aarch64-linux, arm-linux, and the two -cross ones) has shipped
bin/ppc* with ZERO .pas members since v54, exactly like the win64 tarball.
Unpack one and use $VP_DIR/bin/<name> and this cannot reach you.

The exposure is the GIT CHECKOUT used as $VP_DIR, where the binary is a build
product living next to its own sources and where bin/ does not exist at all.
For that case, run:

    dist/linux-bin-layout.sh            # populate <tree>/bin from <tree>/compiler
    dist/linux-bin-layout.sh --check    # verify only; touches nothing

It copies the consumer-facing compilers (ppcx64, ppcross386, ppcrossa64,
ppcrossarm, and the ppcrossaarch64 alias) into <tree>/bin, then PROVES the
property by compiling a trivial program through the installed binary and
asserting the compiler source directory is absent from its unit path -- with
the negative control run first, so a pass cannot be vacuous.
Exit 0 = clean, 1 = the tree is bad, 2 = the check itself could not run.

TWO THINGS THAT LOOK LIKE SHORTCUTS AND ARE NOT
-----------------------------------------------
A SYMLINK DOES NOT WORK.  FPC resolves the executable to its target before
computing exepath, so bin/ppcx64 -> ../compiler/ppcx64 prints
"Using unit path: .../vibepascal/compiler/" and reproduces the hazard in full.
Measured: 20 hits via the symlink, identical to running the original; 0 via a
real copy.  A hard link fails the other way -- a rebuild writes a new inode, so
the link silently stops tracking the compiler you just built.

Which means the copies GO STALE.  bin/ is in .gitignore (upstream FPC's, twice),
so its contents are not committed and cannot be; re-running
linux-bin-layout.sh after a compiler build is part of the deal, and --check
reports a stale copy by md5 rather than letting you ship the wrong compiler.

================================================================
A CORRUPT .PPU ON THE FLOOR: WHAT RECOVERS, AND WHAT DOES NOT
================================================================
Added cy1116 (2026-09-11).  Measured on the shipped v57 Linux compiler,
md5 6a460e0e02cc3ef71313aa5040c1934e, against
packages/aspell/units/x86_64-linux/aspelldyn.ppu (55291 B) with the unit's
SOURCE also on the search path -- units and sources side by side, which is the
shape a real build tree has.

A killed build, a full disk or an interrupted copy leaves a damaged unit file
behind.  v57 made the compiler FAIL on one instead of spinning forever (see
ppu-truncation-check.sh).  This section is the next question: you have the bad
unit and the sources are right there -- what gets you back?

THE TWO CORRUPTION SHAPES DO NOT BEHAVE THE SAME
------------------------------------------------
    zero-byte .ppu   -> rebuilt from source, exit 0.  Self-heals.
    truncated .ppu   -> Fatal: Invalid PPU-File entry: 0, exit 1.  Hard stop,
                        and the source sitting right beside it does not help.

That asymmetry is deliberate and it is not going to change.  A zero-length file
carries no header to disagree with, so the reader rejects it cleanly and the
compiler falls through to the source.  A SHORT READ, by contrast, is an error
and v57 makes that error sticky -- which is the entire point of the fix.  The
alternative would be to rebuild silently over a half-written unit, and silent
recovery from unknown damage is worse than a stop.

A PLAIN RETRY NEVER CLEARS A TRUNCATED UNIT
-------------------------------------------
Measured: three consecutive identical compiles, exit 1 every time, the file
untouched at its truncated length each time.  Re-running the build is not a
remedy and no number of attempts makes it one.  The compiler will rebuild a
unit it cannot FIND; it will not rebuild one it can find but cannot READ.

BUT IT IS RECOVERABLE, AND THE RECOVERY IS ONE rm
-------------------------------------------------
    rm the partial .ppu   (or the whole units/<target> directory)
    re-run the build

Measured: exit 0, and the rebuilt unit is BIT-FOR-BIT what a from-scratch build
of that unit produces.  So this is a stop, not a loss -- do not reach for a
re-roll from clean, and do not go looking for a compiler bug.

Two controls behind that claim, because "it rebuilt something" is not the same
as "it rebuilt the right thing":
  * The rebuild is independent of the damage.  Zero-byte-healed, truncated-
    then-deleted, and simply-absent all produce the SAME md5
    (a07199db4a3cf44459e22fd05a76893c) -- so the corruption does not influence
    the result at all.  Repeated runs and -Cn/-O2 variation give that same md5.
  * It is ABI-identical to the unit we shipped: same size (55291 B), same
    Checksum (60286495), same Interface Checksum (60286495), same Indirect
    Checksum (DD7A3B44), and every dependency CRC equal.  Two bytes of 55291
    differ from the 2026-08-18 shipped copy (at offsets 51 and 55189); they are
    not any checksum and they are not caused by -Cn or -O2, and the shipped
    copy was built by fpmake with an older compiler, which is reason enough.
    We did not isolate which build-context field they are.  It is not a
    corruption signal.

A TRAP FOR ANYONE GATING A BUILD ON LOG TEXT
--------------------------------------------
The zero-byte self-heal prints this and still exits 0:

    Error:  Invalid header size 0 (expecting 40)
    Error:  Invalid header size 0 (expecting 40)

Both halves of that are correct.  compiler/ppu.pas:299 emits it through
do_comment(V_Error, ...) -- a diagnostic channel that prints AT error verbosity
but does not increment the compiler's error count -- so the build genuinely
succeeded and exit 0 is the honest answer.

The consequence is real for tooling, in both directions:
  * A gate that greps a log for "Error" will call this healthy green build a
    failure.  Use the EXIT CODE to decide pass/fail.
  * A gate that looks only at the exit code will never learn that a unit was
    silently rebuilt mid-roll.  That Error line is the only notice you get.

PROVING IT ON YOUR OWN TREE
---------------------------
    dist/ppu-corruption-recovery-check.sh <compiler> <target> <a-real.ppu> \
        <unit-source-dir> <rtl-unit-dir>

    e.g. dist/ppu-corruption-recovery-check.sh compiler/ppcx64 x86_64-linux \
            packages/aspell/units/x86_64-linux/aspelldyn.ppu \
            packages/aspell/src rtl/units/x86_64-linux

Six checks, ~0.7 s, exit 0 = recovery behaves as described above, 1 = it does
not, 2 = the harness could not run (which says nothing about the compiler).
It asserts each claim on this page, including the two controls -- that an
INTACT unit is still loaded rather than rebuilt over, and that the source
fallback is reachable at all, without which none of the other results mean
anything.  Self-tested against the pre-v57 compiler, which it reports as
HANG / 5 of 6 / exit 1, so a pass is not vacuous.
